main.title: NieR Replicant ver.1.22474487139...
main.summary: A remaster of the Replicant version called Nier Replicant ver.1.22474487139... was released internationally for PlayStation 4, Xbox One, and Windows in 2021.

cards.heading: The original and the 2021 remaster
cards.text: NieR Replicant ver.1.22474487139... is the 2021 remaster of the Replicant version of Nier, released internationally for PlayStation 4, Xbox One and Windows. Cavia's original action RPG appeared in 2010. Japan received Replicant with a younger protagonist on PlayStation 3 and Gestalt with an older protagonist on Xbox 360; the latter became the international Nier on both consoles.

cards.heading: Reception of two editions
cards.text: Nier was released to mixed reception; reviewers praised the story, characters, and soundtrack and were mixed in their opinions of how well the disparate gameplay elements were connected. The execution of some gameplay elements was criticized, notably the side quests, and the graphics were regarded as substandard. Despite this, the game acquired acclaim among players over time, becoming a cult classic. The 2021 remaster was released to positive reception, with praise for the graphical and gameplay improvements. The original Nier sold 500,000 copies, while the updated version sold over 2 million copies worldwide. A sequel developed by PlatinumGames, titled Nier: Automata, was released in 2017.

main.title: New Pokémon Snap
main.subtitle: A camera on the way through Lental
main.summary: New Pokémon Snap is Bandai Namco Studios' photography adventure, released for Switch on 30 April 2021.

cards.heading: A camera on the way through Lental
cards.text: New Pokémon Snap is Bandai Namco Studios' photography adventure, released for Switch on 30 April 2021. Joining Professor Mirror's research team, the player travels through the Lental region in an automated vehicle and photographs wild Pokémon. The fixed route leaves attention free to follow behavior across the surrounding habitat. A creature partly hidden in vegetation or interacting with another can become the reason to turn the camera away from an obvious subject, making observation and timing the central actions of the expedition.

cards.heading: Wait for another kind of behavior
cards.text: Returning to a course raises its research level and can reveal different Pokémon and interactions. Nighttime routes change the same habitat again. New tools provide ways to influence the scene and create another photographic opportunity, while the rating system distinguishes the rarity of behavior as well as the quality of a picture. Learning a route therefore means remembering what happens and noticing how it changes. A familiar stretch can supply a photograph that was impossible to anticipate during the first quiet ride through it.

cards.heading: A research album built by returning
cards.text: The laboratory connects the courses to the growing research record, with photographs reviewed and collected into an album. Editing and online sharing extend the life of a favorite shot beyond the trip that produced it. Directed by Haruki Suzaki, the game develops the observation-based premise of the 1999 Nintendo 64 original around detailed habitats and a larger range of behavior. A free update added further courses and Pokémon in August 2021, giving the return journey more places in which to wait for an unexpected moment.

main.title: Returnal
main.subtitle: The Roguelike That Turns Death into Editing
main.summary: Housemarque released Returnal for PlayStation 5 on April 30, 2021, bringing decades of arcade sensibility into a narrative roguelike structure.

cards.heading: The Roguelike That Turns Death into Editing
cards.text: Housemarque released Returnal for PlayStation 5 on April 30, 2021. The roguelike shooter follows Selene after a crash on Atropos: death returns her to the wreck while the surrounding world changes. Rapid movement, changing weapons and dense projectile patterns shape each attempt. Fragments of story and permanent discoveries accumulate as she repeatedly explores the planet.

cards.heading: Every Death Re-Edits the Planet
cards.text: The ship remains Selene's starting point after death, but rooms, rewards and threats are rearranged. Much of the current equipment disappears, while knowledge and some permanent progress survive. Players use what they have learned to respond to a new route. Selene's repeated awakening also makes this cycle part of the story she is trying to understand.

cards.heading: Bullet Hell Meets Three-Dimensional Movement
cards.text: Coloured projectiles and attack signals fill three-dimensional arenas. Dashing, jumping and sprinting help Selene cross those patterns while continuing to fire. Weapons favour different distances, but all require attention to enemy attacks and positioning. Avoiding damage depends on reading the space and moving through it rather than staying behind cover.

cards.heading: New Hardware Becomes Part of Perception
cards.text: DualSense feedback suggests rain and surfaces, while adaptive triggers distinguish weapon functions. Positional 3D sound helps locate threats outside the centre of the screen. These cues supplement the action visible in the arena, giving players more ways to judge their surroundings while moving quickly.

main.title: Resident Evil Village
main.subtitle: Resident Evil Carries Horror into a Distorted European Fairy Tale
main.summary: Capcom released Resident Evil Village outside Japan on May 7, 2021, with Japan following a day later.

cards.heading: Resident Evil Carries Horror into a Distorted European Fairy Tale
cards.text: Capcom released Resident Evil Village outside Japan on May 7, 2021, with Japan following a day later. The game keeps the first-person viewpoint of Resident Evil 7 but changes scale, rhythm and imagery. Instead of the domestic isolation of the Baker house, it builds a village, a castle and territories controlled by very different antagonists. Ethan Winters remains the vulnerable point of view, while the series combines survival horror, action and European folklore in a structure that is almost an anthology.

cards.heading: From Corridor to Village
cards.text: Resident Evil 7 rebuilt fear around tight spaces, pursuits and limited resources. Village keeps the first-person view but opens the scale. The central village links areas with different tones and allows players to revisit earlier places with new keys or tools. That structure supports more frequent action without erasing exploration. The player moves among sieges, quiet rooms, treasure hunts and denser fights, creating a balance that recalls both the seventh game and the offensive pressure of Resident Evil 4.

cards.heading: Four Territories, Four Forms of Fear
cards.text: Each territory changes Ethan's immediate problem. Castle Dimitrescu combines pursuit with a multilevel Gothic setting; House Beneviento largely removes combat; Moreau's area centres on water and bodily horror; and Heisenberg brings machinery and heavier action. The central village links these encounters through Ethan's search for his daughter.

cards.heading: RE Engine and the Material of Horror
cards.text: RE Engine renders worn wood, snow, stone, cloth, metal and skin at the close range of a first-person camera. Ordinary rooms and monstrous figures share this detailed treatment. The familiar textures of the village and castle help establish places the player studies carefully before their dangers become apparent.

main.title: Famicom Detective Club
main.subtitle: Two early mysteries return in a new form
main.summary: Famicom Detective Club's Switch remakes bring The Missing Heir and The Girl Who Stands Behind to a new audience, released on 14 May 2021.

cards.heading: Two early mysteries return in a new form
cards.text: Famicom Detective Club's Switch remakes bring The Missing Heir and The Girl Who Stands Behind to a new audience, released on 14 May 2021. Originally written for the Famicom Disk System in 1988 and 1989, the two adventures follow a young investigator through murders and unsettling local stories. Mages rebuilt their presentation with illustrated scenes and performances. The player advances through conversations and examination, gradually connecting an apparent supernatural threat to the people and events that can be investigated within each community.

cards.heading: Ask again with another piece of evidence
cards.text: Commands such as asking, examining, showing an item and moving to another location structure the inquiry. Looking closely at a scene can reveal an object or a reason to return to a conversation. Progress often comes from reconsidering a subject after another discovery changes its meaning. The Missing Heir begins with the investigator suffering memory loss while examining a death in the Ayashiro family. The Girl Who Stands Behind returns to an earlier case, giving the pair a shared cast but a different point in the investigator's life.

cards.heading: Nintendo’s detective stories reach another audience
cards.text: Yoshio Sakamoto's original writing drew on detective fiction, horror cinema and the command-based Japanese adventure tradition. The 2021 editions made the stories officially available outside Japan for the first time, with Takeshi Abo contributing the remakes' music. They preserve the act of assembling a case through repeated attention to testimony and detail while changing how its people and places are presented. That return also renewed the series itself, leading eventually to a completely new investigation in Emio – The Smiling Man.

main.title: Mass Effect Legendary Edition
main.summary: Mass Effect Legendary Edition is a compilation of the video games in the Mass Effect trilogy: Mass Effect (2007), Mass Effect 2 (2010), and Mass Effect 3 (2012).

cards.heading: The trilogy in one collection
cards.text: Mass Effect Legendary Edition is a compilation of the video games in the Mass Effect trilogy: Mass Effect (2007), Mass Effect 2 (2010), and Mass Effect 3 (2012). Developed by BioWare and published by Electronic Arts, the compilation was released on May 14, 2021, for PlayStation 4, Windows, and Xbox One.  All three games were remastered, with visual enhancements, technical improvements, and gameplay adjustments. Mass Effect, the first game of the trilogy, received more extensive upgrades than its counterparts, specifically with regard to graphics, combat mechanics, vehicle handling, and loading times.

cards.heading: Remastering while preserving the experience
cards.text: Development on the Legendary Edition commenced in 2019 under the direction of Mac Walters, who previously served as lead writer for Mass Effect 2 and Mass Effect 3. BioWare decided to approach the project as a remaster as opposed to a remake in order to preserve the original trilogy experience. Legendary Edition received very positive reviews from video game publications, who praised the enhanced experience of the first game in addition to the convenience and scope of the overall package. Minor criticism was aimed at the extent of the gameplay and visual changes in certain regards.

main.title: Biomutant
main.subtitle: Biomutant Builds an Open World Around Mutation and Reuse
main.summary: Experiment 101 and THQ Nordic released Biomutant for PC, PlayStation 4 and Xbox One on May 25, 2021.

cards.heading: Biomutant Builds an Open World Around Mutation and Reuse
cards.text: Experiment 101 and THQ Nordic released Biomutant for PC, PlayStation 4 and Xbox One on May 25, 2021. The open-world action RPG follows an anthropomorphic creature through a post-apocalyptic landscape. Mutations change abilities, scavenged parts become equipment and martial arts combine with weapons in combat. Factions, moral choices and environmental dangers shape the journey.

cards.heading: The Character Is a Problem of Adaptation
cards.text: Character creation connects physical appearance with statistics. Later biological mutations and powers associated with contamination expand the available abilities. Exploring another zone can therefore provide a new way to adapt the protagonist to its hazards. Growth changes both the character's capabilities and the form visible on screen.

cards.heading: Weapons Are Assembled Objects, Not Whole Finds
cards.text: Weapon crafting combines parts such as bases, grips and barrels. An unwanted object may still contain a component useful for another design. Players can preserve those pieces and assemble equipment from the technological remains scattered across the world. The resulting weapons visibly retain their improvised construction.

cards.heading: The Open World Mixes Fable and Industrial Ruin
cards.text: Colourful forests and creature settlements stand alongside abandoned industrial structures. Polluted zones and the Tree of Life link environmental conditions to the places the player needs to explore. Moving between these areas reveals different hazards as well as the contrast between surviving nature and earlier industry's remains.
